mgmt.config.http.allowInsecureLocalAcces: Allow insecure access via local IP

When HTTPS is used along side a domain, depending on your networking configuration, it is possible that your server is not receiving direct local connections.
This option allows you to also access your Cosmos admin using your local IP address, like ip:port.
You can already create ip:port URLs for your apps, but this will make them HTTP-only.

This option is not recommended as it exposes your server to security risks on your local network.
Your local network is safer than the internet, but not safe, as devices like IoTs, smart-TVs, smartphones or even your router can be compromised.
If you want to have a secure offline / local-only access to a server that uses a domain name and HTTPS, use Constellation instead.

mgmt.constellation.forceReformText: Use this only when this network has permanently lost the majority of its manager nodes and configuration has become read-only. It rebuilds the cluster around this server alone: the other managers are removed and must be re-enrolled from scratch, and until they are, they can no longer change any configuration. Your devices, users, certificates and settings are kept. Note that a removed server keeps the configuration it already holds, so if one of them was lost or compromised, rotate your certificates, API tokens and stored credentials afterwards. This cannot be undone.
mgmt.constellation.resetText: This will completely reset the network, and disconnect all the clients. You will need to reconnect them. This cannot be undone.

mgmt.constellation.setup.dnsText: This is a DNS that runs inside your Constellation network. It automatically rewrites your domains DNS entries to be local to your network, and also allows you to do things like block ads and trackers on all devices connected to your network. You can also add custom DNS entries to resolve to specific IP addresses. This DNS server is only accessible from inside your network.

mgmt.constellation.setup.hostnameInfo:
This are your Constellation hostnames, that the app will use to connect. This can be a mixed of domain name (for dynamic IPs) and IPs.
If you are using a domain name, this needs to be different from your server's hostname. Whatever the domain you choose, it is very important that you make sure there is a A entry in your domain DNS pointing to this server. If you change this value, you will need to reset your network and reconnect all the clients!

mgmt.deployments.modeHelp: Fixed runs an exact number of replicas. Autoscale lets the scheduler move between min and max based on the CPU/RAM load of the nodes running the deployment. Fill runs one replica on EVERY eligible node — use the Tags field to choose which nodes.
mgmt.deployments.modeFillBare: Fill — bare (scales 1 to all tagged nodes)
mgmt.deployments.modeFillEmpty: Fill — empty (scales from zero to all tagged nodes)
mgmt.deployments.fillModeHelp: Full always runs one replica on every eligible node. Bare scales with load between a single replica and every eligible node (same CPU/RAM thresholds as Autoscale). Empty is Bare with lazy containers: the idle replica is stopped and started again by the next request, so the deployment scales from zero.
mgmt.deployments.fillModeEmpty: Empty (load-based, scale from zero with lazy containers)
mgmt.deployments.minMaxInvalid: Min replicas must be at least 1 and not exceed max replicas
mgmt.deployments.strategyHelp: How the scheduler picks nodes for this deployment. Least-busy falls back to round-robin when resource monitoring is disabled on any node.
mgmt.deployments.tagsHelp: Comma-separated list. Only nodes whose device tags include ALL of these will be eligible. Leave empty to allow any node.
mgmt.deployments.composeInfo.templatesBo: Use ${node_name}, ${node_mode}, ${node_ip}, ${deployment_name} in env values, labels, command, entrypoint, hostname, and volume sources/targets. Each node substitutes its own values on apply. Unknown placeholders are left literal, so $VAR references intended for the container's own shell pass through.
mgmt.deployments.composeInfo.storageBody: ${storage.NAME} expands to /mnt/cosmos-storage-NAME, the host path where the matching RCLONE remote is mounted. RCLONE config is cluster-synced — a remote configured on any node is usable here. Declare required remotes in the deployment's "storage" field for a fail-fast check on apply; missing remotes return a clear error without starting containers.
mgmt.deployments.monitoringNodeNote: Resource metrics are collected per node: only the replicas running on this node are shown here.
mgmt.deployments.deleteConfirm: Delete deployment "{{name}}"? The scheduler will stop and remove all of its replicas across the cluster.
mgmt.deployments.brokenNodesDesc: These nodes failed repeated deploys and are skipped by the scheduler until cleared, which can leave deployments under-replicated.

mgmt.databases.unrestrictedWarning: The database will accept connections from any network that can reach this node, not just the Constellation.

mgmt.databases.backup.repositoryChangeWa: Changing the repository starts a fresh one: the snapshots already taken stay in the old repository and will no longer be listed or restorable here.
mgmt.databases.backup.retentionHelp: restic forget flags applied by the cleanup schedule.
mgmt.databases.backup.disabledWarning: Scheduled backups are paused. The repository and its existing snapshots are kept, and "Backup now" still works.
mgmt.databases.backup.saveError: Could not save the backup settings
mgmt.databases.backup.runStarted: Backup started. The snapshot will appear in the list once it completes.

mgmt.databases.backup.restoreDesc: Creates a NEW managed database from snapshot {{snapshot}} ({{time}}) of "{{source}}". The source instance is left untouched.
mgmt.databases.backup.restoreAll: Restore every database in the snapshot
mgmt.databases.backup.databasesListHelp: Comma-separated list of the application databases to restore from this snapshot.
mgmt.databases.backup.portHelp: Left empty, a free port is picked on the home node.
mgmt.databases.backup.credentialsOnceHin: These passwords are shown once and are not recoverable afterwards. Copy them now; the only way back is rotating them.
mgmt.databases.logicalEmpty: No application database yet. Create one below to give an application its own database and role.
mgmt.databases.dangerZoneDesc: Deleting the instance stops and removes its container on the home node. The data volume is kept unless you choose to delete it too.
mgmt.seaweedfs.nameHelp: 3 to 27 lower-case letters and digits. Used to derive the filer database, the deployments and the backup tags.
mgmt.seaweedfs.createDesc: Creates an S3-compatible SeaweedFS cluster: three pinned masters, one volume server on every tagged node, and a filer + S3 gateway behind the load balancer. A managed database is provisioned automatically for the filer metadata.
mgmt.seaweedfs.managersHint: Requires at least 3 constellation managers (NATS cluster mode).
mgmt.seaweedfs.tagsHelp: Comma-separated. A volume server runs on every constellation node carrying ALL of these tags.
mgmt.seaweedfs.tagMatch.none: No node carries these tags. Nothing would be scheduled: no volume server, no filer, and the S3 endpoint would never come up. Tag at least one node first, or use a tag that already exists.
mgmt.seaweedfs.tagMatch.short: Only {{matched}} matching node is up, but this instance asks for {{need}} filers. It will run with fewer until more nodes carry the tags.
mgmt.seaweedfs.tagMatch.down: {{down}} matching node(s) are not currently reachable. Nothing is placed on them until they are back.
mgmt.seaweedfs.filerReplicasHelp: How many filer + S3 gateways to run. They are load balanced, so two or more keeps S3 available while one restarts.
mgmt.seaweedfs.indexModeHelp: leveldb keeps the needle index on disk (lower memory); memory keeps it in RAM (faster, but every restart rebuilds it).
mgmt.seaweedfs.replicationHelp: How many extra full copies of every volume are kept on other nodes. Fixed once the instance is created.
mgmt.seaweedfs.replication.000: no copy — data is lost with its node
mgmt.seaweedfs.replication.001: one extra copy on another node (survives losing one node)
mgmt.seaweedfs.replication.002: two extra copies on other nodes (survives losing two nodes)
mgmt.seaweedfs.replication.noneWarning: This instance keeps a single copy of every volume: losing a node loses the data on it, and no maintenance job can bring it back.
mgmt.seaweedfs.volumeSizeLimitHelp: Size at which a volume is considered full and a new one is allocated.
mgmt.seaweedfs.minFreeSpaceHelp: Percent (e.g. 10) or absolute size (e.g. 20GiB) a volume server keeps free before it stops accepting writes.
mgmt.seaweedfs.maxStorageHelp: How much disk this instance may use on each volume server. 0 means unlimited. Enforced in whole volumes (cap ÷ volume size limit), so the real ceiling rounds down to a multiple of the volume size.
mgmt.seaweedfs.storage.title: Storage
mgmt.seaweedfs.storage.collectedAt: Measured by the monitoring job at {{when}}.
mgmt.seaweedfs.storage.noData: No measurement yet — the monitoring job records this on its next run.
mgmt.seaweedfs.storage.noNodes: No volume server answered on the last monitoring run.
mgmt.seaweedfs.storage.listTooltip: Used by this instance, and disk still free across its {{nodes}} volume server(s) ({{free}}).
mgmt.seaweedfs.storage.saved: Storage cap saved. The volume servers restart one node at a time to pick it up.
mgmt.seaweedfs.storage.saveError: Could not save the storage cap
mgmt.seaweedfs.imageHelp: The exact SeaweedFS image every tier runs.
mgmt.seaweedfs.unrestrictedWarning: The S3 endpoint will accept requests from any network that can reach the cluster, not just the Constellation.
mgmt.seaweedfs.emptyDesc: Create an instance to get an S3-compatible endpoint backed by the constellation nodes you tag.
mgmt.seaweedfs.status.waitingForNodesToo: The instance was created, but its tags match no node: there is nowhere to run a volume server or a filer, so the S3 endpoint will never come up. Tag a node, or none of this cluster's storage is reachable.
mgmt.seaweedfs.placement.title: Placement
mgmt.seaweedfs.placement.desc: The volume tier runs one server on every node matching the instance tags; the filers are placed on the same set.
mgmt.seaweedfs.placement.noneMatched: No node carries these tags, so nothing is scheduled and nothing ever will be until a node is tagged. This is why the instance never finishes configuring its S3 credentials.
mgmt.seaweedfs.placement.filerCapped: The filer target is capped at {{desired}} because only that many nodes match the tags (the instance asks for {{configured}}).
mgmt.seaweedfs.quorumLostTooltip: Fewer than half the masters are up: the cluster has lost quorum and cannot allocate or write volumes until a master comes back or is replaced.
mgmt.seaweedfs.deleteConfirm: Delete object storage "{{name}}"? Its masters, volume servers and filers are torn down on every node.
mgmt.seaweedfs.deletePurgeData: Also purge data volumes on every node
mgmt.seaweedfs.deletePurgeWarning: This destroys every object stored in this cluster on every node. There is no way back.
mgmt.seaweedfs.deleteLeftovers: The instance was removed, but parts of the teardown failed: {{notes}}
mgmt.seaweedfs.masters.title: Masters
mgmt.seaweedfs.masters.desc: Three masters pinned to constellation managers. They hold the volume topology, so a majority has to be up for the cluster to accept writes.
mgmt.seaweedfs.masters.replaceDesc: Re-provisions the master currently pinned to "{{device}}" onto another manager. Use this when the node is not coming back.
mgmt.seaweedfs.masters.newDeviceHelp: Leave empty to let the cluster pick an eligible manager itself.
mgmt.seaweedfs.masters.replaceStarted: The master is being replaced. The tier rolls out over the next few minutes.
mgmt.seaweedfs.s3.title: S3 access
mgmt.seaweedfs.s3.configuringDesc: The S3 credentials are still being written to the filer. The endpoint will start accepting them shortly.
mgmt.seaweedfs.s3.noEndpoints: No filer is answering yet, so there is no endpoint to show.
mgmt.seaweedfs.s3.primaryEndpointHelp: Preferred endpoint: it matches the cluster hostname, so TLS validates. The other entries are per-filer addresses inside the Constellation.
mgmt.seaweedfs.s3.secretKeyHelp: Full access to every bucket on this instance.
mgmt.seaweedfs.filerDB.title: Filer database
mgmt.seaweedfs.filerDB.desc: The filer metadata lives in the managed database "{{db}}" — manage its backups in the Databases tab.
mgmt.seaweedfs.jobs.title: Maintenance jobs
mgmt.seaweedfs.jobs.desc: Scheduled cluster maintenance. Schedules are 6-field crontabs (seconds first) and run from the constellation leader.
mgmt.seaweedfs.jobs.ecDesc: By default every volume is kept as two full copies on different nodes (replication 001), so a lost node is recoverable. Erasure coding (EC) is a cost saver on top of that: cold, full volumes are re-encoded as 10 data + 4 parity shards spread across nodes, keeping the data recoverable at ~1.4x its size instead of 2x. Converting a volume temporarily needs about twice its size free, which is why it is off by default and skipped below a minimum free-disk percentage.
mgmt.seaweedfs.jobs.repackDesc: Runs automatically whenever erasure coding is on: deleted objects inside an erasure-coded volume cannot be vacuumed in place, so repacking is the only way that space is ever reclaimed.
mgmt.seaweedfs.jobs.saveError: Could not save the maintenance jobs
mgmt.seaweedfs.backup.title: Metadata backups
mgmt.seaweedfs.backup.unconfiguredDesc: The filer metadata is not backed up. Configure a restic repository to take scheduled snapshots of it. The objects themselves are protected by replication, not by this backup.

mgmt.sales.remote.title: Unlock Cosmos Premium and connect your Cosmos to remote storage, and share your folders
mgmt.sales.remote.description: Cosmos Advanced Storages unlocks powerful networking options for your server. Remote Storage is a functionality that allows you to connect to dozens of cloud providers and protocols like Dropbox, Google Drive, FTP, etc... In order to see your files on your server. With this function, Cosmos allows you to attach those storage to containers as folder (instead of using local folders). It also allows you to backup your files and containers to those storages automatically. Network Shares allow you to share your folders on the network, using protocols like NFS, FTP, etc... For example, using Cosmos you could in a few click create a static site from a folder in your Dropbox, back it up automatically to OneDrive, and locally share the folder to your local network via FTP for edition.
mgmt.sales.remote.features.0: Connect to dozens of cloud providers and protocols as if they were local folders
mgmt.sales.remote.features.1: Backup your files and containers to those storages automatically
mgmt.sales.remote.features.2: Easy setup and management through the Cosmos interface
mgmt.sales.remote.features.3: Attach those storage to containers as bind or volume directly
mgmt.sales.remote.features.4: Share your local AND remote folders on the network using protocols like NFS, FTP, etc...
mgmt.sales.remote.features.5: Monitor your storage usage and health
mgmt.sales.backup.title: Unlock Cosmos Premium and safeguard your data with advanced backup solutions
mgmt.sales.backup.description: Cosmos Backup System brings enterprise-grade data protection to your home server. Our comprehensive backup solution ensures your valuable data is always safe and recoverable. With automated scheduling, you can back up your containers, configurations, and files to any storage destination, whether local or cloud-based. The system supports incremental backups to save space and bandwidth, while maintaining multiple versions of your data. Through Cosmos's intuitive interface, you can easily set up complex backup strategies, monitor backup status, and restore data with just a few clicks. For instance, you could automatically backup your critical databases nightly to local storage, maintain weekly snapshots in cloud storage, and restore any version instantly if needed.
mgmt.sales.backup.features.0: Schedule automated backups of containers, volumes, and configurations
mgmt.sales.backup.features.1: Support for incremental backups to optimize storage space and transfer time, with deduplication
mgmt.sales.backup.features.2: No vendor-locking: you can always restore your backups without Cosmos as it is using Restic under the hood
mgmt.sales.backup.features.3: One-click restore process for quick disaster recovery
mgmt.sales.backup.features.4: Fully encrypted backups for your data security
mgmt.sales.backup.features.5: Choose between local, remote, or hybrid backup destinations
mgmt.sales.constellation.title: Unlock Cosmos Premium and use Constellation: Your Secure Gateway Home
mgmt.sales.constellation.description: Constellation is a powerful VPN based technology that allows you to securely access your home server from anywhere, without the need to open ports on your router. Keep your data safe and your connections secure with our state-of-the-art encryption technology.
mgmt.sales.constellation.features.0: Securely access your home server from anywhere in the world
mgmt.sales.constellation.features.1: No need to open ports, reducing potential security vulnerabilities*
mgmt.sales.constellation.features.2: Encrypted connections keep your data safe from prying eyes*
mgmt.sales.constellation.features.3: Easy setup and management through the Cosmos interface
mgmt.sales.constellation.features.5: Block ads and trackers on all devices

mgmt.backup.confirmBackupDeletion: Are you sure you want to delete this backup?
mgmt.backup.createBackupInfo: Configure backup settings. All backups are encrypted using AES-256. You can safely re-use the same destination folder (repository) for many backups, the backed up files will be de-dupped, and Cosmos use a tagging system to tell backups appart in the repository. Cosmos uses Restic under the hood, so you can restore your backups even without Cosmos. Creating a backup folder in a distant remote folder takes time. It's normal do not panic!
mgmt.backup.scheduleForget: Crontab Forget Schedule (how often to clean up old backups)
mgmt.backup.restore.success: Restore operation has been queued. You can monitor the progress in the tasks log on the top right.
mgmt.backup.restore.summary: You are about to restore {count} file(s)/folder(s). This will overwrite existing files.
mgmt.backup.autoStopContainers2: Automatically Stop Containers using that folder before backup/restore operations (Recommended for database data folders and config folders, not required for media and documents)
trust.benefits: Ensure encrypted communication between your browser and our services
Eliminate security warnings while maintaining a secure connection
Have full control over your certificate infrastructure
Fix issues with IOS apps such as Emby that don't support self-signed certificates
trust.selfSignedInfo: This is only needed if you use a self-signed certificate, or if you have .local / IP based routes. Otherwise, you can ignore this!
trust.title: Understanding Self-Signed Certificates
trust.intro.first: HTTPS uses certificates to encrypt data between your browser and the sites you visit. In your home server, you have the choices between a public certificate from a Certificate Authority (CA) which is trusted by all browsers, or a self-signed certificate which is not trusted by default. A public certificate requires a full domain name, that is why Cosmos fallsback to a self-signed certificate when an IP, or a .local domain is used. In order to ensure maximum security, you can setup Cosmos as a CA, in case you need to use a self-signed certificate. This will tell your browser to trust the certificates issued by Cosmos.
trust.intro.second: While self-signed certificates aren't usually recommended for public-facing websites, they can be a secure choice for internal applications and development environments. By properly installing our Certificate Authority (CA) certificate, you can:
trust.installation.title: Certificate Installation
trust.installation.followInstructions: Follow the instructions below to install the certificate on your device.

trust.noInstall.title: Nothing to Install
trust.noInstall.message: You are not currently using any self-signed certificate. There is no need to install any certificate.
trust.platforms.windows: Choose "Place all certificates in the following store"
Click "Browse" and select "Trusted Root Certification Authorities"
trust.platforms.macos: Add the certificate to the "System" keychain

sudo.required: Enable Admin privileges with the button on the top right to use this function
mgmt.servapps.compose.credentialsRequire: The Compose editor requires access to container credentials (environment variables, secrets). Please enable Admin privileges using the button on the top right to view and edit the Compose configuration.
mgmt.servapps.compose.credentialsDenied: The Compose editor requires access to container credentials (environment variables, secrets). Your current role does not have permission to view credentials.
mgmt.registry.dangerZoneDesc: Deleting a registry removes its record and all of its package metadata. Stored blobs are kept unless you explicitly purge them.
mgmt.registry.nameHelp: 3 to 27 lower-case letters and digits. It becomes the bucket name and, for Docker, the first path segment of every image.
mgmt.registry.typeImmutable: The type cannot be changed later: the metadata layout and the protocol both hang off it.
mgmt.registry.typeDesc.docker: OCI container images, pushed and pulled with the docker CLI or buildx.
mgmt.registry.typeDesc.npm: npm packages, published with npm publish and installed with npm install.
mgmt.registry.typeDesc.static: Versioned static websites uploaded as zip archives, each served on its own URL with instant rollback.
mgmt.registry.typeDesc.generic: Any files, organised as package / version / file: installers, tarballs, models, build artifacts. Uploaded from this UI or with curl, downloaded by URL.
mgmt.registry.typeDesc.pypi: Python packages, published with twine, uv or poetry and installed with pip from a private index.
mgmt.registry.createDesc: A registry is typed storage: a bucket, a quota and a protocol. It is not reachable on its own — publishing it takes an access, which the next step offers to create for you.
mgmt.registry.storage.title: Storage
mgmt.registry.storage.label: Where should the blobs live?
mgmt.registry.storage.instanceHelp: A bucket is created inside this managed SeaweedFS instance. Its credentials are resolved at use time, so rotating them is picked up for free.
mgmt.registry.storage.noManaged: No managed object storage exists yet. A local folder works for a single node; create an Object Storage instance first if you want the registry to survive a node loss.
mgmt.registry.storage.localWarning: A local folder lives on ONE node. Only that node can serve this registry, and losing it loses the data.
mgmt.registry.storage.externalS3Label: Use an external S3 bucket instead
mgmt.registry.storage.externalS3Warning: Every pull reads from this bucket, so egress is billed by your provider and latency is whatever the round-trip is. Managed object storage keeps both inside the constellation.
mgmt.registry.storage.bucketHelp: Leave empty to generate one from the registry name.
mgmt.registry.storage.secretKeyHelp: Stored server-side and never returned by the API.
mgmt.registry.storage.pathHelp: Leave empty to use a folder inside the Cosmos configuration directory.
mgmt.registry.quotaHelp: Maximum stored size. Leave empty or 0 for unlimited.
mgmt.registry.usageUpdated: Counters last reconciled {{at}}. They are maintained by every serving node and by the sweep, so treat them as close, not exact.
mgmt.registry.gcDesc: Garbage collection walks the blob store and removes anything no version references. Blobs younger than 24 hours are always kept, whether or not anything points at them.
mgmt.registry.gcStarted: Garbage collection of {{name}} started. The result will appear in the events.
mgmt.registry.notPublished: No access publishes this registry yet, so nothing can reach it. Create one in the Accesses tab.
mgmt.registry.deleteConfirm: Delete the registry {{name}}? Its record and all of its package metadata go with it.
mgmt.registry.deleteBlocked: This registry is still published by: {{accesses}}. Remove it from those accesses first — the server will refuse otherwise.
mgmt.registry.deletePurgeWarning: Every image, package and archive in this registry will be erased. This cannot be undone.
mgmt.registry.deleteLeftovers: The registry was deleted, but part of the teardown failed: {{notes}}
mgmt.registry.emptyDesc: A registry is typed storage for container images, npm packages, static sites or generic files, hosted inside your own constellation.
mgmt.registry.emptyHint: Create one, then publish it on a hostname by adding an access.
mgmt.registry.offerAccessDesc: An access is the endpoint clients point at: its own hostname, its visibility, and the deploy tokens that open it. You can skip this and add one later.
mgmt.registry.offerAccessTokenNote: One deploy token with pull and push scope will be minted and shown once.
mgmt.registry.offerAccessTypeNote: This will be a {{type}} endpoint. An access serves exactly one registry type, so only other {{type}} registries can be added to it later.
mgmt.registry.access.nameHelp: 3 to 27 lower-case letters and digits. Only used to identify the endpoint in this UI and in the events.
mgmt.registry.access.createDesc: An access publishes one or more registries on a hostname. The protocols it answers follow from the types of the registries you pick — there is nothing to choose here.
mgmt.registry.access.createdNoToken: The access was created but the deploy token could not be minted. Add one from the access details.
mgmt.registry.access.registriesHelp: One access serves one type. Pick a registry and the others narrow to the same type — several docker registries can share an endpoint (they are told apart by the path), an npm or generic access exposes exactly one.
mgmt.registry.access.typeLockedHelp: This is a {{type}} endpoint: only {{type}} registries can be added to it. Create a second access for another type.
mgmt.registry.access.mixedTypeError: An access serves exactly one registry type. Remove the registries that do not match, or create a second access for them.
mgmt.registry.access.npmLimitError: An npm access exposes exactly one registry: npm URLs carry no namespace segment to tell two of them apart.
mgmt.registry.access.genericLimitError: A generic access exposes exactly one registry: its URLs are /package/version/file, with no segment to tell two registries apart.
mgmt.registry.access.pypiLimitError: A PyPI access exposes exactly one registry: pip is pointed at /simple/, with no segment to tell two registries apart.
mgmt.registry.access.hostHelp: The hostname clients point at. Docker only ever addresses a registry by hostname over TLS, so this has to resolve to your server.
mgmt.registry.access.hostDetailHelp: Docker, npm and every other client address this endpoint by this hostname.
mgmt.registry.access.hostChangeHelp: Changing the hostname republishes the route. Clients configured with the old one will stop resolving.
mgmt.registry.access.internalHelp: Only reachable from inside the constellation. Requests arriving from anywhere else are refused.
mgmt.registry.access.publicHelp: Reachable from the public internet. Pushes still need a deploy token.
mgmt.registry.access.anonPullWarning: Anyone on the internet will be able to pull everything this endpoint exposes, without a token.
mgmt.registry.access.tagsHelp: Comma-separated. Only nodes carrying ALL of these tags serve this endpoint. Leave empty — the default — to serve it from every node.
mgmt.registry.access.tagMatch.none: No node carries these tags. This access would be published nowhere: its hostname would answer on no node and every push and pull to it would fail.
mgmt.registry.access.tagMatch.down: {{down}} matching node(s) are not currently reachable and are not serving this endpoint.
mgmt.registry.access.noServingNodes: No node is serving this yet
mgmt.registry.access.deleteKeepsData: The registries it published, and everything stored in them, are untouched. Only this endpoint and its deploy tokens go.
mgmt.registry.access.dangerZoneDesc: Deleting the access takes the endpoint down at once. Clients pointing at this hostname will stop resolving.
mgmt.registry.access.emptyDesc: A registry is only reachable through an access: the hostname clients point at, its visibility, and the deploy tokens that open it.
mgmt.registry.access.emptyNoRegistries: Create a registry first — an access has to expose at least one.
mgmt.registry.token.title: Deploy tokens
mgmt.registry.token.desc: A deploy token authenticates docker, npm, curl and CI uploads against this endpoint. Only its hash is stored, so the value is shown once at mint.
mgmt.registry.token.none: No deploy token on this access yet.
mgmt.registry.token.mintDesc: The token is scoped to the registries this access exposes, and nothing else.
mgmt.registry.token.nameHelp: Letters, digits, '-' and '_' only. It ends up in URLs and in copy-pasted configuration.
mgmt.registry.token.noScopeDefault: With no scope ticked the token is minted with both pull and push.
mgmt.registry.token.copyWarning: Copy it now. Only its hash is stored, so this is the only time it will ever be shown.
mgmt.registry.token.revokeConfirm: Revoke the deploy token {{name}}? Anything using it stops working.
mgmt.registry.token.revokeDelay: It stops working on this node immediately and on the others within a few seconds. A Docker session token already handed out stays valid for the rest of its five-minute life.
mgmt.registry.snippet.title: How to use this endpoint
mgmt.registry.snippet.desc: One block per protocol this access speaks. Replace the placeholder names; the hostnames and registry paths are already the real ones.
mgmt.registry.snippet.npmLoginTitle: Point npm at this endpoint with this token
mgmt.registry.snippet.pypiLoginTitle: Publish with twine using this token
mgmt.registry.snippet.staticNote: Static sites are uploaded through the management API, not through this hostname: each site is served on its own URL, configured in the registry's details.
mgmt.registry.snippet.unknownTypes: The exposed registries could not be resolved, so no snippet can be built. Refresh the page.
mgmt.registry.static.title: Static sites
mgmt.registry.static.noSites: No site in this registry yet.
mgmt.registry.static.uploadDesc: The zip is stored as one immutable deployment. Activating it is a separate, instant pointer move — which is also how a rollback works.
mgmt.registry.static.versionHelp: Leave empty to name the deployment after the current UTC timestamp.
mgmt.registry.static.hostHelp: The hostname this site is served on. Each site gets its own route, independent of any access.
mgmt.registry.static.spaHelp: Unknown paths fall back to index.html instead of answering 404, which is what a client-side router needs.
mgmt.registry.static.tagsHelp: Comma-separated. Leave empty to serve the site from every node.
mgmt.registry.static.deleteSiteConfirm: Delete the site {{site}} and its {{count}} deployments? The route goes down immediately.
mgmt.registry.static.deleteVersionConfir: Delete the deployment {{version}} of {{site}}? The archive is reclaimed by the next garbage collection.
mgmt.registry.generic.title: Packages
mgmt.registry.generic.noPackages: No package in this registry yet.
mgmt.registry.generic.uploadDesc: Every selected file is stored under its own name inside one version. A file that already exists in that version is refused: publish a new version instead.
mgmt.registry.generic.packageNameHelp: Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'. It becomes the first URL segment.
mgmt.registry.generic.versionHelp: Leave empty to name the version after the current UTC timestamp. 'latest' always resolves to the newest version.
mgmt.registry.generic.deletePackageConfi: Delete the package {{package}} and its {{count}} versions? The stored files are reclaimed by the next garbage collection.
mgmt.registry.generic.deleteVersionConfi: Delete the version {{version}} of {{package}}? 'latest' moves to the newest remaining version.
mgmt.registry.generic.deleteFileConfirm: Delete the file {{file}} from {{package}} {{version}}? If it is the last file, the version goes with it.
mgmt.registry.generic.ciNote: This uploads through the management API with a deploy token. The access publishing this registry also serves the same packages at https://<access host>/<package>/<version>/download — see the access's details for the URLs.
mgmt.registry.contents.clientNote: A {{type}} registry is browsed and published with its own client tooling, through the endpoint of an access that exposes it. There is nothing to upload here.
